q: In Grade 11, the angular displacement, angular velocity and angular ____ of an object in circular motion have been learnt.
e: The textbook lists angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular acceleration as the rotational variables learnt in Grade 11.

q: In Grade 11, the angular ____, angular velocity and angular acceleration of an object in circular motion have been learnt.
e: Angular displacement is the first of the three rotational variables introduced in Grade 11.

q: In this chapter, the concepts and equations for rotational motion under constant angular acceleration and ____ acceleration will be studied.
e: The chapter focuses on rotational motion under constant angular acceleration and centripetal acceleration.

q: It is expected that students will differentiate between the circular motion and ____ motion.
e: Differentiating between circular and rotational motion is a key learning outcome of the chapter.

q: It is expected that students will examine rotational motion under constant angular ____.
e: Examining rotational motion under constant angular acceleration is a stated learning outcome.

q: It is expected that students will deduce the relations between angular and ____ quantities.
e: Students are expected to deduce the relations between angular and linear quantities.

q: It is expected that students will understand the ____ acceleration.
e: Understanding centripetal acceleration is one of the core learning outcomes.

q: It is expected that students will distinguish between the uniform circular motion and ____ circular motion.
e: Distinguishing between uniform and nonuniform circular motion is a key learning outcome.

q: In a circular motion, the object just moves in a ____.
e: The textbook defines circular motion as an object just moving in a circle.

q: Artificial satellites going around the earth at a constant height is an example of ____ motion.
e: Artificial satellites orbiting the earth are given as an example of circular motion.

q: In rotational motion, the object rotates about an ____.
e: Rotational motion is defined as an object rotating about an axis.

q: The rotation of earth about its own axis creates the cycle of day and ____.
e: The earth's rotation about its axis creates the cycle of day and night.

q: The motion of the blades of a ____ is an example of rotational motion.
e: The motion of fan blades is listed as an example of rotational motion.

q: The motion of a ____ wheel in an amusement park is an example of rotational motion.
e: A Ferris wheel in an amusement park is given as an example of rotational motion.

q: A ____ body is a body that does not deform or change shape.
e: A rigid body is defined as a body that does not deform or change shape.

q: That is, no matter how the body moves, the ____ between any two particles within the body remains constant.
e: For a rigid body, the distance between any two particles remains constant regardless of its motion.

q: For a rigid body, the distance between any two ____ within the body remains constant.
e: The constant distance applies to any two particles constituting the rigid body.

q: If a rigid body is in rotational motion, all the particles constituting it undergo ____ motion about a common axis.
e: All particles of a rigid body in rotational motion undergo circular motion about a common axis.

q: When an object (rigid body) rotates, it can speed up or slow ____.
e: A rotating rigid body can change its speed by speeding up or slowing down.

q: During these time intervals, its angular velocity is changing therefore it has an angular ____.
e: A changing angular velocity means the object possesses an angular acceleration.

q: If its angular velocity changes at a constant rate, then we can say that the angular acceleration is constant and the motion is called the rotational motion under constant angular ____.
e: Motion with a constant rate of change in angular velocity is called rotational motion under constant angular acceleration.

q: Angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular acceleration are examples of ____ variables.
e: These three quantities are classified as rotational variables.

q: Rotational variables are applied to analyze the rotational motion for a rigid body about a fixed ____ under a constant angular acceleration.
e: The analysis in this section focuses on a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis.

q: For an object that rotates with a constant angular acceleration, the ____ equations for rotational motion can be derived in terms of the angular displacement, angular velocity and angular acceleration of the object at any instant of time.
e: Kinematic equations are derived for rotational motion under constant angular acceleration.

q: The initial angular speed is the magnitude of angular velocity of the object at $t = $ ____.
e: Initial angular speed is defined at time $t=0$.

q: The equation for angular speed is $\omega = \omega_0 + $ ____.
e: This is the kinematic equation relating final angular speed, initial angular speed, angular acceleration, and time.

q: Average angular speed is, $\frac{\omega + \omega_0}{____}$.
e: The average angular speed is the arithmetic mean of the initial and final angular speeds.

q: The equation for angular displacement is $\theta = \omega_0 t + \frac{1}{2} $ ____.
e: This is the kinematic equation for angular displacement under constant angular acceleration.

q: The relation between angular speed and angular displacement is $\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + $ ____.
e: This is the time-independent kinematic equation for rotational motion.

q: The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are the same as those for linear motion, with the angular quantities replaced with corresponding ____ ones.
e: The rotational kinematic equations are direct analogues of the linear kinematic equations.

q: The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are analogous to equations for constant acceleration in ____ motion.
e: Table 1.1 shows the direct analogy between linear and angular kinematic equations.

q: The relations between linear quantities and angular quantities for circular motion have been studied in Grade ____.
e: The textbook notes that these relations were previously studied in Grade 11.

q: All particles of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move in a ____ path.
e: Every particle in a rotating object follows a circular path.

q: All particles of the body move in a circle lying on a plane that is ____ to the axis, such that the centre of rotation lies on the axis.
e: The plane of the circular path for any particle is perpendicular to the axis of rotation.

q: For a rotating rigid body, the centre of rotation lies on the ____.
e: The centre of the circular path for all particles is located on the axis of rotation.

q: The linear distance of a particle of a rotating object measured along the ____ is $s$.
e: The linear distance $s$ is measured along the arc of the circular path.

q: The arc length $s$ subtends an angle $\theta$ at the ____.
e: The angular displacement $\theta$ is the angle subtended by the arc at the origin.

q: The relation between arc length $s$ and angular displacement $\theta$, measured in radian, is $s = $ ____.
e: This is the fundamental geometric relationship between arc length and angular displacement.

q: In the relation $s = r\theta$, the angular displacement $\theta$ is measured in ____.
e: The formula $s = r\theta$ requires the angle to be measured in radians.

q: The instantaneous angular velocity $\omega$ of rotational object is the ____ for all the particles comprising the object.
e: All particles of a rigid rotating body share the same instantaneous angular velocity.

q: The relation between the magnitude of the linear velocity $v$ and the angular velocity $\omega$ of a particle is $v = $ ____.
e: This equation correctly relates linear velocity to angular velocity and radius.

q: In the relation $v = r\omega$, the angular velocity $\omega$ is measured in ____ per second.
e: Angular velocity must be in radians per second for this relation to hold.

q: The relation $v = r\omega$ applies to ____ particle of the rotational object.
e: The textbook states that this relation applies to every particle of the rotational object.

q: Since the direction of linear velocity is tangent to the path, the linear velocity is also called ____ velocity.
e: Linear velocity in circular motion is tangential to the path, hence the name tangential velocity.

q: If the magnitude of the angular velocity of a rotating object changes, the magnitude of ____ velocity will also change.
e: Because $v = r\omega$, a change in $\omega$ necessitates a change in linear velocity $v$.

q: If the magnitude of the angular velocity of a rotating object changes, the magnitude of linear velocity will also change and the object will have a ____ acceleration.
e: A changing linear velocity magnitude results in a tangential acceleration.

q: The direction of tangential acceleration is always ____ to the circular path.
e: Tangential acceleration acts along the tangent to the circular path of the particle.

q: The tangential acceleration $a_T$ relates to angular acceleration $\alpha$ by the equation $a_T = $ ____.
e: This is the correct equation relating tangential acceleration to angular acceleration.

q: Angular acceleration $\alpha$ is measured in radian per second ____.
e: The standard unit for angular acceleration is radian per second squared.

q: The tangential acceleration of a rotating object is a measure of how fast the ____ velocity changes.
e: The textbook explicitly defines tangential acceleration as the measure of how fast tangential velocity changes.

q: Table 1.2 expresses the relation between the linear and ____ quantities.
e: Table 1.2 summarizes the relations between linear and rotational quantities.

q: The direction of the angular velocity vector is ____ to the plane of rotation, and along the axis of rotation.
e: This correctly describes the spatial orientation of the angular velocity vector.

q: The direction of the angular velocity vector is perpendicular to the plane of rotation, and along the ____ of rotation.
e: The angular velocity vector lies along the axis of rotation.

q: The direction of angular velocity is usually specified by the ____ rule.
e: The right-hand rule is used to determine the direction of the angular velocity vector.

q: Wrap the right hand around the axis of rotation so that the ____ are pointing in the direction of rotation.
e: This is the correct procedure for applying the right-hand rule to angular velocity.

q: When using the right-hand rule, wrap the right hand around the axis of rotation so that the fingers point in the direction of ____.
e: The fingers must curl in the same direction as the object's rotation.

q: The ____ points in the direction of the angular velocity vector.
e: In the right-hand rule, the extended thumb indicates the direction of the angular velocity vector.

q: When the angular velocity is increasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the ____ direction as the angular velocity.
e: An increasing angular velocity means the angular acceleration is in the same direction as the angular velocity.

q: When the angular velocity is decreasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the ____ to the angular velocity.
e: A decreasing angular velocity indicates that angular acceleration opposes the direction of angular velocity.

q: An object that moves in a circle at constant speed $v$ is said to experience ____ circular motion.
e: This is the exact definition of uniform circular motion provided in the textbook.

q: The ____ of the velocity remains constant in uniform circular motion, but the direction of the velocity continuously changes.
e: The speed (magnitude of velocity) is constant in uniform circular motion.

q: In uniform circular motion, the magnitude of the velocity remains constant, but the ____ of the velocity continuously changes as the object moves around the circle.
e: The direction of the velocity continuously changes as the object moves around the circle.

q: The change in direction of velocity constitutes an ____.
e: Because velocity is a vector, a change in its direction means there is an acceleration.

q: Thus, an object revolving in a circle is continuously ____, even when the speed remains constant.
e: The continuous change in the direction of velocity means the object is continuously accelerating.

q: Average acceleration has been defined as $\vec{a} = \frac{\Delta \vec{v}}{____}$.
e: This is the standard definition of average acceleration.

q: When $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the ____ acceleration can be obtained.
e: Taking the limit as the time interval approaches zero yields the instantaneous acceleration.

q: During the time interval $\Delta t$, the object covers a distance $\Delta s$ along the arc which subtends an angle ____.
e: The small distance $\Delta s$ along the arc subtends a small angle $\Delta \theta$.

q: The change in the velocity vector is denoted by ____.
e: The change in the velocity vector $\vec{v}_2 - \vec{v}_1$ is represented by $\Delta \vec{v}$.

q: If $\Delta t$ is very small, then $\Delta s$ and $\Delta \theta$ are also very small, and, $v_2$ will be almost ____ to $v_1$.
e: For an infinitesimally small time interval, the initial and final velocity vectors are almost parallel.

q: When $\Delta t$ approaches zero, $\Delta \vec{v}$ will be essentially perpendicular to the velocity vectors and points toward the ____ of the circle.
e: In uniform circular motion, the infinitesimal change in velocity points radially inward toward the centre.

q: The triangle CAB is geometrically ____ to the vector triangle of the change in velocity.
e: The textbook uses the geometric similarity of these triangles to derive the centripetal acceleration formula.

q: In uniform circular motion, the magnitudes of the initial and final velocities are equal, so $v_1 = v_2 = $ ____.
e: The constant speed in uniform circular motion is denoted by $v$.

q: The limit of $\frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}$ as $\Delta t$ approaches zero is the linear ____ of the object.
e: The derivative of arc length with respect to time gives the linear speed.

q: Acceleration directed toward the centre of the circle is called centripetal acceleration or ____ acceleration.
e: The textbook uses both terms to describe the inward-directed acceleration.

q: Centripetal acceleration is denoted by ____.
e: The standard symbol for centripetal acceleration is $a_c$.

q: The magnitude of the centripetal acceleration can be determined by the equation $a_c = $ ____.
e: This is the standard formula for the magnitude of centripetal acceleration.

q: Substituting $v = r\omega$ into the centripetal acceleration equation gives $a_c = $ ____.
e: Replacing $v$ with $r\omega$ in $a_c = \frac{v^2}{r}$ yields $a_c = r\omega^2$.

q: In the equation $a_c = r\omega^2$, the term $\omega$ represents the angular ____.
e: The symbol $\omega$ stands for angular velocity.

q: For uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration vector points towards the ____ of the circular path.
e: Centripetal acceleration is always directed radially inward toward the centre.

q: For uniform circular motion, the linear velocity vector is ____ to the path.
e: The linear velocity vector is always tangent to the circular path.

q: Hence, the centripetal acceleration and linear velocity are ____ to each other at every point in the path.
e: The radial direction of acceleration and tangential direction of velocity are always perpendicular.

q: In ____ circular motion, an object is moving in a circular path with a varying speed.
e: Varying speed is the defining characteristic of nonuniform circular motion.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, the varying speed is the magnitude of ____.
e: Speed is defined as the magnitude of the velocity vector.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, the angular speed of the object is changing and the object experiences the angular ____.
e: A changing angular speed means the object has an angular acceleration.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, the angular ____ of the object is changing.
e: Because the linear speed is varying, the angular speed is also changing.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, the angular acceleration gives rise to the ____ acceleration.
e: The angular acceleration is responsible for the change in the magnitude of the linear velocity, creating tangential acceleration.

q: The tangential acceleration is ____ to the circle.
e: Tangential acceleration acts along the tangent to the circular path.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, there is tangential acceleration in addition to ____ acceleration.
e: Both centripetal acceleration (due to changing direction) and tangential acceleration (due to changing speed) are present.

q: An object in nonuniform circular motion has a resultant acceleration that is the vector ____ of the centripetal and tangential accelerations.
e: The total linear acceleration is the vector sum $\vec{a} = \vec{a}_c + \vec{a}_T$.

q: The resultant acceleration in nonuniform circular motion is the vector sum of the centripetal and ____ accelerations.
e: The two components of acceleration in nonuniform circular motion are centripetal and tangential.

q: The equation for the resultant acceleration vector is $\vec{a} = \vec{a}_c + $ ____.
e: This is the vector equation for the total acceleration.

q: Unlike tangential acceleration, centripetal acceleration is present in ____ uniform and nonuniform circular motion.
e: Any circular motion requires centripetal acceleration to change the direction of velocity.

q: The two acceleration vectors $\vec{a}_c$ and $\vec{a}_T$ are ____ to each other.
e: Radial (centripetal) and tangential directions are always perpendicular.

q: The centripetal acceleration vector $\vec{a}_c$ is in the ____ direction.
e: Centripetal acceleration is directed radially inward.

q: The tangential acceleration vector $\vec{a}_T$ is in the ____ direction.
e: Tangential acceleration is directed along the tangent to the path.

q: The resultant acceleration points at an ____ between $\vec{a}_c$ and $\vec{a}_T$.
e: As the vector sum of two perpendicular components, it points at an angle between them.

q: The magnitude of resultant acceleration $a$ is $a = \sqrt{a_c^2 + $ ____ }.
e: Because the two components are perpendicular, the Pythagorean theorem is used to find the magnitude.

q: The direction of resultant acceleration $a$ is given by $\tan \phi = \frac{a_T}{____}$.
e: This trigonometric relationship defines the angle of the resultant acceleration vector relative to the radial direction.

q: If the angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the angular ____ is constant.
e: A constant rate of change of angular velocity defines constant angular acceleration.

q: Rotational motion under constant angular acceleration occurs when the angular velocity changes at a constant ____.
e: The defining condition is that the angular velocity changes at a constant rate.

q: The acceleration directed towards the centre of the circular path is called ____ acceleration.
e: This is the summary definition of centripetal acceleration.
